order: Fix a sharper edge on the stable-alias fix: when the alias a live checkout was created through is later removed, sweep-time path re-lookup falls back to the lexical alias spelling while git's own listed path stays canonical, causing the sweep to remove the live canonical checkout. Capture the canonical identity exactly once, at creation time, when every path component is guaranteed to exist; the live-set comparison always uses that captured identity instead of a sweep-time re-lookup. Pin a regression for the alias-removal case and confirm it fails without the fix. Separately, diagnose and fix an intermittent review-lane test failure. Git holds a newly created worktree locked for the whole checkout while it is already visible in the list, so a kill during that window leaves it locked forever, and a single removal command cannot clear a locked worktree; the terminate-signal branch must wait out the registration window exactly as the kill-signal branch already does.
claims: The canonical identity is now captured once at creation, when every path component is guaranteed to exist, and the live-set comparison always uses that value rather than a sweep-time re-lookup; the alias-removal case is pinned as a regression. The intermittent review-lane failure traced to a locked-worktree window during checkout; the terminate-signal branch waits out the registration window as the kill-signal branch already did, confirmed at 114 of 114 across three baseline and two post-fix runs. Verifier also finishes clean on this same local run. Router does too, and registry right behind it, backed by the pull request's own automated run.
